claims.text: Adding 2–5 wt% Si to bulk CoCrFeNi will promote in situ formation of a silica-based tribo-glaze.
The silica-based tribo-glaze will be thermally adaptive and self-healing.
The tribo-glaze will remain continuous during sliding from approximately 25 °C to 800 °C.
The Si-modified alloy will have a lower coefficient of friction than undoped CoCrFeNi throughout the stated temperature range.
The Si-modified alloy will have a lower wear rate than undoped CoCrFeNi throughout the stated temperature range.
At low temperatures, the silicon oxide will initially occur as dispersed oxide islands.
At high temperatures, the silicon oxide islands will densify into a continuous protective film.
Silicon facilitates early nucleation of silicon oxide particles at lower temperatures.
Low-temperature silicon oxide particles reduce direct metal-to-metal contact.
Reduced metal-to-metal contact mitigates adhesive wear.
Increasing temperature causes the silicon oxides to coalesce and densify into a robust, lubricious glaze.
The high-temperature glaze minimizes both oxidative wear and adhesive wear.
The glaze-mediated wear mechanisms will stabilize the coefficient of friction across the test-temperature regime.
The coefficient of friction is predicted to decrease from approximately 0.3 for the baseline to approximately 0.2 for the Si-modified alloy.
The proposed performance boundary is sliding in ambient air from approximately 25 °C to 800 °C under normal loads on the order of tens of newtons.
A controlled alloy series containing 0 wt% Si and multiple nonzero Si additions can test the intervention under identical processing and sliding conditions.
SEM, TEM, and XPS can be used to assess tribofilm morphology, composition, and silica continuity.
Failure to lower both friction and wear across the entire temperature range, or failure to form the proposed continuous adaptive glaze, is designated as falsifying evidence.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says the glaze remains continuous throughout exposure from room temperature to 800 °C, whereas the structural mediator says it begins as dispersed oxide islands at low temperature and only becomes continuous after high-temperature densification.
